title: Copy to the supervising physician within 24 hours of issuance
rule_summary: Under 105 CMR 700.003(G)(10) the pharmacist PROVIDES A COPY of an initial prescription OR a modification OR a discontinuation of a prescription TO THE SUPERVISING PHYSICIAN WITHIN 24 HOURS OF ITS ISSUANCE, UNLESS MORE URGENT NOTIFICATION IS REQUIRED UNDER THE CIRCUMSTANCES. The duty sits on the pharmacist, the period runs from issuance, and it reaches a modification or a discontinuation as well as an initial prescription.
exam_relevance: Tests the only clock in 105 CMR 700.003(G): 24 hours measured from issuance, owed by the pharmacist to the supervising physician, reaching modifications and discontinuations, and shortened where the circumstances require more urgent notification.

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations

numeric_facts.fact: time to provide the supervising physician with a copy of an initial prescription, modification or discontinuation
numeric_facts.conditions: from issuance, unless more urgent notification is required under the circumstances

exceptions: Where more urgent notification is required under the circumstances, the 24-hour period is not the standard; the proviso shortens the time rather than extending it.
common_confusions: The 24 hours run from issuance of the prescription, not from the pharmacist's next contact with the physician and not from dispensing.
The duty reaches a modification or a discontinuation as well as an initial prescription.
The copy goes to the supervising physician; the subparagraph names no other recipient.
verification_notes: Read in the current official publication of 105 CMR 700.000 at the Department of Public Health download link on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule rather than by changing an existing record, so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
